_comment: THE place to add a language. Read by src/i18n/locales.ts (app) and scripts/lib/locales.js (build: sitemap, prerender, the <head> redirect snippet). Nothing else keeps its own language list. See locales.ts for the helpers built on top of this.
_choiceStorageKeyComment: localStorage key holding an EXPLICIT language choice (the switcher). Deliberately not i18next's own language cache, which also gets written when the language changes merely because a prefixed URL was opened. The <head> redirect snippet reads only this key.
_xDefaultComment: Where a visitor whose language matches no locale is sent. English, per the brief.
_localizedRoutesComment: Marketing paths that genuinely exist in EVERY locale, i.e. whose copy is translated. Only these get a /<prefix> URL and tr<->en hreflang pairs. Today that is the landing page alone: /about, /contact, /careers, /blog and the four legal pages are hardcoded English with no translation layer, so giving them an /en twin would publish two URLs with byte-identical English content and tell Google they are translations of each other. When one of those pages is actually translated, add its path here — that is the whole change.
_unlocalizedLocaleComment: The real content language of the marketing pages that are NOT in localizedRoutes. /about, /contact, /careers, /blog and the legal pages are written in English only, so <html lang> must say en on them even though the site's default locale is tr — claiming tr would mislabel an English document for screen readers and search engines. Each page that gets translated moves into localizedRoutes and stops depending on this.
